featured_reviews.name: Aamna Quraishii
featured_reviews.review_text:
Got their croissants and chocolate eclairs for some weekend indulgence, and what a pleasantly unexpected surprise this has been!
The butter croissant is flaky, buttery deliciousness. The chocolate croissant is all that plus the most scrumptious, mouth watering chocolate filling!

Don’t be fooled by soft, bready looking packs in store. Take them home and warm in a hot oven for 2-3 mins; leave to cool and they will be the best croissants you will have bought at a bakery in the city. Crispy on the outside with those layers and a good bite inside!

The eclair was polished off with no time for a photo but again, delicious chocolate coating and cream filling, soft base which can be warmed and crisped on a pan if you like it toasted.

Portions are massive and well priced.

I bought the croissants end of day on a Friday and they tasted fresh through the weekend stored at room temp; eclair in the fridge.

Quick billing at the late hour but they do get very busy during peak.
Their cookies and palmiers are legendary; looking forward to trying other pastries and tiramisu soon!

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m extremely disappointed with J Hearsch & Co. in Bandra. Despite being an old and reputed establishment, their quality, service, and overall experience have gone drastically downhill.

To begin with, the staff—especially the owner—were shockingly rude. It’s as if they believe they’re the only bakery that exists just because they’ve been around a while. Sadly, that attitude is exactly why this was my last visit.

Yes, the place has a legacy, but that doesn’t mean you stop upgrading where it matters. Instead of improving service and food quality, they’ve only focused on increasing their prices while everything else has degraded. The quantity has reduced significantly, and the quality is no longer what it used to be.

Here’s what I ordered:
•	Chicken Burger
•	Chicken Samosa
•	Mutton Samosa
•	Mutton Puff
•	Chicken Roll
•	Lime Water

The burger used to come with wafers in a decent box—now it’s wrapped in flimsy paper. The lime water, which once had good quantity for a reasonable price, is now expensive (₹100) and barely enough. Most items were just okay, but not worth the price or the hassle.

There is no seating, no parking, and still, customers are expected to follow a long list of rules. Instead of focusing on unnecessary regulations, they should really work on their customer service, which is currently pathetic.

Honestly, there’s no point in putting in so much effort to visit a place where the staff behaves rudely and the food no longer justifies the hype or price. I won’t be returning, and I certainly won’t recommend this bakery to anyone. Keep your attitude—I’ll take my business elsewhere.

**Texture and Taste:**
With a gentle tear, the buns revealed their tender crumb. Soft, yet resilient, they yielded to my touch. Each bite was a revelation—a symphony of flavors. The spices played their part: cinnamon hummed, nutmeg chimed, and the faint zest of orange lingered. The currants, plump and sweet, added a delightful surprise. And oh, that cross! It was more than mere decoration; it held the promise of resurrection.
**Packaging:**
The packaging was more than practical—it was an invitation to slow down, savor, and appreciate life's simple pleasures. A nod to tradition, a whisper of love.
**Conclusion:**
As I savored the last crumbs, I realized that Daily Bread's Hot Cross Buns were more than a pastry; they were a connection to centuries past. They carried the warmth of family gatherings, the sweetness of shared laughter, and the hope of renewal. So, here's to Daily Bread N Foods—for crafting not just buns, but memories.

featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Anverali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Deliciae by Bunty Mahajan: Mango Biscoff Cheesecake = Summer in a Slice*

Deliciae never misses with desserts, but the *Mango Biscoff Cheesecake* is next-level indulgence. If you think mango and Biscoff sounds risky, this will convert you.

*Presentation*: It arrives looking like art. A perfect round slice with that golden mango glaze on top, a generous dusting of Biscoff crumbs, and a caramelized Biscoff biscuit perched on the side. The layers are clean and distinct even before the first bite. You can tell it’s been set with care, not rushed.

*Taste & Texture*: This is where it becomes addictive. The base is a thick, buttery Biscoff crust that holds up without crumbling everywhere. It gives you that warm, spiced caramel note in every forkful. The cheesecake layer is insanely smooth and creamy, with a light tang that cuts through the sweetness. Then comes the mango: real Alphonso pulp, not artificial essence. It’s fresh, tropical, and balances the Biscoff beautifully so nothing feels cloying. The top glaze adds a subtle fruity brightness. Together it’s sweet, spiced, tangy, and lush.

*Overall Experience*: Each bite gives you multiple textures. Crumbly base, silky cheesecake, soft mango layer, and that little crunch from Biscoff crumbs on top. It’s rich but not heavy, and somehow feels both decadent and summery at once. Portion size is generous enough to share, though you won’t want to.

*Vibe at Deliciae*: The patisserie itself matches the dessert. Elegant, pastel, with display counters that make you want everything. Staff are super helpful and package it beautifully if you’re taking away. No soggy cheesecake disasters here.

*Verdict*: Mango + Biscoff sounds like a weird collab that should not work, but Deliciae makes it iconic. This cheesecake is indulgent, balanced, and wildly photogenic. Easily one of the best fusion desserts I have had this season.

*Pro tip*: Pair it with their cold coffee. Thank me later.

Already craving my next slice. If you’re a cheesecake or mango person, skip everything else and get this first.

Every bite was an explosion of decadent chocolate-hazelnut flavor, perfectly balanced, not overly sweet, and incredibly indulgent. It truly lived up to its “Divine” name!

This cake didn’t just taste extraordinary; it made her day truly special. Her smile and excitement said it all – it was the highlight of the gym ! At around ₹2631, it was worth every single rupee for the premium quality, freshness, and joy it brought.
Deliciae By Bunty Mahajan continues to be Mumbai’s best pâtisserie for a reason – flawless execution, timely delivery, and cakes that are as beautiful as they are delicious.
